The four state messages keep four distinct promises and the two the sidecar constrains are exactly right: 'error' says the change could not be CONFIRMED and never claims the write failed, while 'rejected' does assert not-saved as a 4xx licenses. The brief's specific check also passes: this namespace contains no account-policy option label and no policy vocabulary at all, so no second rendering exists. findings.reason: This locale binds 'equipo' to TEAM (glossary line 63: team -> equipo; style-guide/es.md line 29 lists 'equipo (team)'), while 'computer' ships as 'máquina' in 11 of the 17 en values that mention it, including 7 in this same phone relay surface, so this screen renames the very object it is about and its central promise ('changes apply only to this computer') becomes readable as 'changes apply only to this team'.
findings.counter_argument: In fairness: 'equipo' is legitimate Spanish for a computer (equipo informático) and in isolation 'Ajustes del equipo' is a correct rendering of 'Computer settings'. The finding is not that the Spanish is wrong; it is that inside this product 'equipo' already means team, and inside this phone UI the same object is called 'máquina' seven times.
findings.resolution_note: (a) Adopt 'máquina' here, matching the shipped sibling wire.settings.account_policy.error.write_failed ('en esta máquina'). (b) Declare 'equipo' the locale-wide word for computer, which would also require rewriting 7 shipped relay strings plus wire.errors.notifications.store_full and would still collide with glossary line 63. (a) is the cheap, consistent fix.
findings.evidence: Value-only scan of every es catalogue: 11/17 en 'computer' values ship as 'máquina'; 5/17, all in this namespace, use 'equipo'; 1 pre-existing outlier (wire.errors.notifications.store_full). 7 of the 11 'máquina' renderings are inside relay.* itself (relay.health x4, relay.chrome, relay.notifications x2).
